subject: Global transfer DPF addendum and DPA annex clarifications (HARM-2029-001)
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@harmonia-fin.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Oliver Mann <oliver.mann@harmonia-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: DPF evidence + DPA annex clarifications (HARM-2029-001)

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week. As part of our procurement checklist for Harmonia Financial Services we're gathering detailed evidence to validate cross-border transfer safeguards and DPA annex items before we move to legal redlines. Specific asks from our security and privacy reviewers: 

- A consolidated evidence bundle that maps technical controls to the DPF criteria (encryption in transit/at rest, KMS/HSM usage, key ownership and rotation policies).
- A current list of subprocessors with regions and whether they have access to plaintext data.
- Clarify whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed KMS for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Details on routing policies: can traffic be pinned to specific regions or routed to regional fallbacks? We need to understand how model routing could result in cross-border processing.
- Logging and retention: example log schema for inference requests (what PII, IP addresses, cookies are logged) and retention windows; whether audit logs can be exported to our SIEM.
- For the DPA annex: an editable draft we can run through our legal team; highlight any non-negotiable clauses.

Can you provide the above (or an expected delivery date)? We have a submission deadline for our vendor review on 2029-05-10.

Appreciate it — Emily

Emily Carter
Senior Procurement Manager
Harmonia Financial Services
emily.carter@harmonia-fin.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: none

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@harmonia-fin.com>
Cc: Oliver Mann <oliver.mann@harmonia-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 2 May 2029 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: DPF evidence + DPA annex clarifications (HARM-2029-001)

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Quick note to confirm we'll get a consolidated package to you by Friday 2029-05-03 EOD Pacific, with an editable DPA annex draft and the technical evidence bundle. High-level answers inline first, followed by next steps.

1) Evidence bundle: we'll attach a zipped evidence package containing our DPF mapping, encryption technical note, audit-log schema, and subprocessor registry (redacted where required). See attached: redwood_dpf_evidence_bundle_v1.zip.

2) Subprocessors: our current list (see bundle) identifies which subprocessors process non-tokenized inference payloads. Short summary: analytics and observability vendors receive only pseudonymized telemetry by default; storage and backup providers may hold encrypted artifacts. We'll flag any subprocessors that have potentially plaintext access (very limited).

3) BYOK/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments. We offer HSM-backed KMS integrations for Private customers and a BYOK flow for Dedicated (we can provide an ops runbook). We'll include the KMS key rotation policy PDF.

4) Routing and residency: routing policies are configurable per-tenant and per-model. You can pin requests to a region or allow failover to an adjacent region (configurable). For hosted customers default routing may go to the nearest available region; we'll include a routing-policy matrix and sample config.

5) Logging & retention: our standard inference request logs contain request timestamp, model id, tenant id, request token counts, and anonymized request metadata. IP addresses are captured only when explicitly enabled for threat detection and are stored in a separate, access-controlled audit log with a default 90-day retention (configurable). We can provide sample schemas and SIEM export examples.

6) DPA annex editable draft: attached (dpa-annex-draft.docx). Legal will mark optional/non-negotiable clauses.

Next steps: I've looped in Marissa (marissa_cole) for clarifying subprocessor exposure and Kimberly (kimberly_park) for technical controls and the audit-log schema. Expect the full bundle and a short cover note by tomorrow EOD. If you need anything sooner, let me know.

Best,
David
David Kim
Head of Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.inference.com
+1 (650) 555-0122

Attachments: redwood_dpf_evidence_bundle_v1.zip; kms-key-rotation-policy.pdf; dpa-annex-draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.inference.com, kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Harmonia RFP - subprocessor exposure & templates

David / Kimberly — internal draft answers and notes for the evidence bundle (confidential):

- Subprocessor exposure: we have three categories. 1) Storage/backups (encrypted at rest, AES-256), 2) Observability (ingest-only, pseudonymized), 3) Model infra partners (GPU providers) — only encrypted weights and ephemeral cache; no persistent plaintext inference storage. We should mark "Model infra partners" as having no routine access to customer payloads, though they could in an emergency given access controls.

- BYOK: Ops runbook will include HSM attestation steps and key import for Dedicated. For Private deployments we can support customer-managed HSMs behind their VPC peering. Include a short diagram.

- Log schema: attach sample lines for SIEM export. Important fields: timestamp, tenant_id, model_id, request_id, token_counts, decision_flags (e.g., routed_to_fallback=true), and a separate audit index for admin actions. IP address/headers only in the 'security-audit' index and accessible via an approvals workflow.

- DPA Annex: legal comments in-line on clause 4.2 (subprocessor notification timing) — propose 30 days notice and emergency access clauses.

I'll drop the internal redlined snippets into the Drive folder; David, can you confirm we can send the unredacted subprocessor registry to Harmonia legal or whether we should produce a redacted vendor list first?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Privacy Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@harmonia-fin.com>
Cc: Oliver Mann <oliver.mann@harmonia-fin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 3 May 2029 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: DPF evidence + DPA annex clarifications (HARM-2029-001)

Hi Emily — attaching the consolidated package (Drive link below and zipped bundle attached). Summary of what's included: 

- redwood_dpf_evidence_bundle_v1.zip: mapping spreadsheet (controls -> DPF criteria), subprocessor registry (redacted column for vendor contracts), encryption technical note, sample routing policy matrix, SIEM export examples (CSV), and sample audit-log schema.
- kms-key-rotation-policy.pdf (key ownership & rotation process for BYOK and Redwood-managed keys).
- dpa-annex-draft.docx (editable, with our legal flags).

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDEF-ghIJkL
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/HARM-2029-001

A few clarifications from the bundle: 
- Subprocessor registry: we intentionally redact contract pricing and some operational contact fields; we can provide an unredacted copy to authorized legal contacts under an NDA if required.
- BYOK/HSM: supported in Dedicated and Private. For Dedicated we support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS or GCP KMS; for Private we can integrate with on-prem HSMs or MKE.
- Routing: tenant-level config flags "region_pin" (strongly recommend for regulated workloads) and "regional_failover". Pinning guarantees no cross-border failover except in manually authorized incidents.
- Logs: IP addresses are captured only in the security-audit index (default disabled). If Harmonia enables IP capture we recommend a 90-day retention with SIEM exports for longer-term storage.

Next step: Oliver, if your legal team can run the enclosed DPA draft and send any redlines by 2029-05-08 we can turn around responses and prepare exec sign-off.

Best regards,
David

Attachments: redwood_dpf_evidence_bundle_v1.zip; kms-key-rotation-policy.pdf; dpa-annex-draft.docx

From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@harmonia-fin.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Oliver Mann <oliver.mann@harmonia-fin.com>
Date: Sat, 4 May 2029 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP: DPF evidence + DPA annex clarifications (HARM-2029-001)

David / team — thanks, received and shared with security & legal. A couple quick follow-ups before we circulate to execs: 

1) If Harmonia enables IP capture in the security-audit index, can Redwood provide an automated SIEM export to our Splunk instance (S3 transfer or syslog) with encryption-in-transit? If so, what are the expected latencies and any egress cost implications?

2) You mentioned model infra partners and ephemeral cache — can you clarify whether KV cache contents are ever persisted to disk in any hosted mode or whether they remain strictly in GPU memory for the hosted offering? This matters for our residency and encryption requirements.

If you can answer these two items today we'll be able to push the bundle to our legal review on Monday.

Thanks — Emily

Emily Carter
Senior Procurement Manager
Harmonia Financial Services
